THEATRE REVIEW THE BAKER'S WIFE

Monday, February 19, 1996

ROBERT CUSHMAN

WRITTEN BY JOSEPH STEIN AND STEPHEN SCHWARTZ Directed by Todd Stewart At the Studio Theatre, Harbourfront, until Feb. 24 Rating: Musical slight but roles charming BY ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail THERE is a category of Broadway show that devotes much of its energy to presenting cross-sections of some kind of enclosed community, real or fantastic. I think of it as the Merry Villagers Musical. It's an unruly category whose denizens, either sentimental or satirical, include Brigadoon, Plain and Fancy, Anyone Can Whistle, Lil Abner and The Most Happy Fella. The masterpiece of the genre, if you don't count Porgy and Bess, is Fiddler on the Roof, which owes much of its power to the staging of Jerome Robbins and, as is less often noted, to the supremely skillful libretto furnished by Joseph Stein.
